newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures open slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures open slightly lower.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures were lower in light, early trade.
September Standard & Poor's 500 contracts eased below the GLOBEX low of 949.15 after dealer buying dried up. Several traders noted active dealer buying at the opening of pit trade.
"We may break lower yet," Kevin O'Brien, a short-term technical analyst at Prudential Securities, said. O'Brien said 946.00 to 947.00 would provide decent support for September.
Other near-term support levels are 942.90 and 941.50, which is last Friday's low, floor traders said.
"When the market really got hit on Friday, people were buying at 941.50," one S&P futures floor trader said.
On Friday, September S&Ps rose more than 10 full points from that level in afternoon trade on Friday.
"The key was the over-the-counter market and Nasdaq," O'Brien said.
The Nasdaq composite will remain a key factor to S&Ps on Monday, traders said.
"Nasdaq has been back-and-forth this morning, but overall it's resilient and that has supported S&Ps," one floor trader said.

Nikkei futures were lower, but some traders said September Nikkeis were due for an upside correction. Resistance is seen at 19,840.00. The contract has retraced losses above near-term resistance at 19,740.0 in light trade.
Fair value for September S&Ps is at 4.85 points to the cash index, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 5.90 points and arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 4.00, floor traders said.

At 0941 CDT/1441 GMT, September S&P 500s were off 4.10 pts at 949.00, Nikkeis fell 105.0 pts to 19,775, KCBT Value Lines were down 2.25 at 838.75, new composites were 1.55 lower at 491.50, Midcap 400s were off 1.40 to 315.50, Russell 2000s lost 0.50 to 414.50, and Nasdaq 1000s were up 1.50 to 1,120.25.
